section_1_complete_textbook_notes.chapter_overview: This chapter investigates line (reflectional) symmetry and rotational symmetry. It details lines of symmetry, mirror halves, center of rotation, order of rotational symmetry n, smallest angle of symmetry (360°/n), and symmetry properties of regular polygons.

detailed_sections.full_textbook_explanation: A shape has line symmetry if a line divides it into two mirror halves that coincide under folding. A regular n-gon has exactly n lines of reflection symmetry.

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: An axis dividing a figure into two mirror-image halves that coincide upon reflection.
mathematical_definitions.example: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.

formulas_and_properties.name: Regular Polygon Symmetry Rule
formulas_and_properties.statement_or_expression: Number of Lines of Symmetry = n
formulas_and_properties.variable_definitions: n = number of equal sides of regular polygon
formulas_and_properties.direct_example: Equilateral triangle (n=3) has 3 lines of symmetry.

detailed_sections.full_textbook_explanation: A figure possesses rotational symmetry if it matches its original appearance after rotation by an angle < 360° around its center. Order n = number of matching positions in 360°. Smallest Angle = 360° / n.

mathematical_definitions.formal_definition: Property where a shape maps onto itself when turned around a center point by an angle less than 360°.

asymmetric_rotation_mastery.concept: Rotational Symmetry without Reflection & Point Groups
asymmetric_rotation_mastery.explanation: Shapes like 3-blade windmills or swastikas have rotational order n > 1 but zero lines of reflection. Regular n-gons possess dihedral symmetry group D_n with n reflection lines and order n rotation.

section_2_step_by_step_algorithms.method_name: Determining Rotational Order and Smallest Angle
step_by_step_instructions: Step 1: Fix center point of rotation.
Step 2: Rotate shape 360° and count matching orientations (Order n).

model_textbook_example.problem: Find smallest rotational angle for Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes).

section_3_in_text_boxes_and_try_these.question_text: Can a shape have rotational symmetry with smallest angle 17°?
section_3_in_text_boxes_and_try_these.complete_solution: No, because 360° / 17° = 21.176..., which is not an integer.
